Fix diffusion correction boundary leakage in OverlandKinematic

At domain boundaries (upper x/y faces), the diffusion correction computed
dh/dx and dh/dy gradients using ghost cell values (h=0), creating artificial
lateral outflow. Lower boundary handlers already skipped the correction,
but upper boundaries did not.

Guard diffusion correction gradient and flux terms with k1x >= 0 / k1y >= 0
checks in both CALCFCN (residual) and CALCDER (Jacobian). When the neighbor
has no physical surface cell, the correction term is zeroed and the flux
reverts to kinematic. Interior patch boundaries (parallel) are unaffected
since top_dat is communicated via ghost exchange.

Substantial changes to met forcing I/O.

NOTE: OLD RUN SCRIPTS MAY NEED MINOR MODIFICATION TO RUN AFTER UPDATE. SEE BELOW FOR DETAILS.

Met forcing for PF.CLM is now read in solver_richards.c and passed to CLM, rather than being read directly by CLM. 
Also, global time keeping (istep) is now done in solver_richards.c and passed to CLM, rather than being done in CLM.
Lastly, #ifdef HAVE_CLM/#endif added in solver_richards.c for code blocks used only by CLM. 

The option of has been added for using 1D (uniform over the domain) or 2D (spatially distributed) met forcing. For 
the 1D case, met forcing is specified as before in a single text file (e.g., narr_1hr.txt). For the 2D case, forcing
data for each time step and variable are specified in separate .pfb files. Met forcing options are specified by the 
following new keys: 

Solver.CLM.IstepStart  -- starting time step of current run (defaults to 1)
                          If run is not a restart, set to 1 
                          If run restarts from previous PF.CLM run, set to 1+endtime of previous run
                          (istep was previously read from CLM restart files and written to global_nt.src at each time step)

Solver.CLM.MetForcing  -- 1D (uniform) or 2D (distributed) met forcing
                          (set to 1D for uniform, 2D for distributed; defaults to 1D)

Solver.CLM.MetFilePath -- path to met forcing data
                          (defaults to run directory)

Solver.CLM.MetFileName -- file name of met forcing data
                          For 1D forcing, this is the full file name (e.g., narr_1hr.txt)
                          For 2D forcing, this is the base file name. Files must be named as follows:
                                <MetFileName>.<Var>.<istep>.pfb      (e.g., nldas.Temp.000001.pfb)
                          where <Var>s are the eight met forcing variables, and 
                                <istep> is the PF.CLM time step since the start of the run (six-digit integer)
                          Currently, <Var>s follow the NLDAS naming convention:
                              shortwave radiation = DSWR
                              longwave radiation  = DLWR
                              precipitation       = APCP
                              air temperature     = Temp
                              U-wind              = UGRD
                              V-wind              = VGRD
                              air pressure        = Press
                              air spec. humidity  = SPFH
                          For any other naming convention, solver_richards.c must be edited.

Parallel NetCDF dataset compression (#267)

Added configurable deflate (zlib) compression capabilities to the NetCDF based writing routines. The possibilities of parallel data compression will only work in combination with the latest NetCDF4 v4.7.4 release.

Two new configuration options can be used:

pfset NetCDF.Compression True Enable deflate based compression (default: False)
pfset NetCDF.CompressionLevel 1 Compression level (0-9) (default: 1)

This work was implemented as part of EoCoE-II project (www.eocoe.eu).

Benchmark tests show that the datasize for regular NetCDF output files could be lowered by a factor of three, in addition, as less data is written to disk, the reduced data size can also lower the overall I/O footprint towards the filesystem. Therefore, depending of the selected setup, the compression overhead can be balanced by reduced writing times.

The resulting NetCDF4 data files, which contain compressed datasets, are still readable by every normal NetCDF4 access mechanic without additional dependenc

Add extended CLM snow parameterization options   Feature/clm snow (#698)

## Summary
Extends CLM snow parameterizations with new rain-snow partitioning
methods, SZA-based melt damping, and configurable fractional snow cover.
**New Features:**
- **Dai (2008) rain-snow partitioning**: Hyperbolic tangent function
fitted to 30 years of global observations
- **Jennings (2018) rain-snow partitioning**: Bivariate logistic
regression using temperature and relative humidity
- **SZA-based snow melt damping**: Reduces melt energy at high solar
zenith angles where CLM underestimates albedo
- **Configurable fractional snow cover**: Adjustable roughness parameter
for frac_sno calculation
- **Configurable temperature thresholds**: SnowTCrit, SnowTLow,
SnowTHigh, SnowTransitionWidth for existing methods
**New Keys (16 total):**
- `Solver.CLM.SnowTCrit`, `SnowTLow`, `SnowTHigh`, `SnowTransitionWidth`
- `Solver.CLM.DaiCoeffA`, `DaiCoeffB`, `DaiCoeffC`, `DaiCoeffD`
- `Solver.CLM.JenningsCoeffA`, `JenningsCoeffB`, `JenningsCoeffG`
- `Solver.CLM.SZASnowDamping`, `SZADampingCoszenRef`,
`SZADampingCoszenMin`
- `Solver.CLM.FracSnoScheme`, `FracSnoRoughness`
**References:**
- Dai (2008) GRL doi:10.1029/2008GL033295
- Jennings et al. (2018) Nature Communications
doi:10.1038/s41467-018-03629-7
- Dang et al. (2019) The Cryosphere doi:10.5194/tc-13-2325-2019
## Test plan
- [x] `clm_snow_dai` - Dai sigmoidal partitioning method
- [x] `clm_snow_jennings` - Jennings bivariate logistic method
- [x] `clm_snow_sza_damping` - SZA-based melt reduction
- [x] All existing CLM snow tests pass

Refactor Zero-Initialization MemSet for Improved Kokkos Performance (#622)

This PR refactors `KokkosMemSet` operations by replacing manual
zero-initialization via `parallel_for `with a more efficient and
portable `Kokkos::deep_copy` on unmanaged memory views. This improves
overall Kokkos performance, simplifies logic, and aligns with modern
Kokkos best practices.

**Summary of Changes:**

- Replaced loop-based based zeroing with `Kokkos::deep_copy` using
unmanaged views.
- Scoped synchronization instead of a global `Kokkos::fence()`.
- Removed alignment-based branching logic, simplifying code and
improving readability.

**Performance Comparison (vs Native CUDA on NVIDIA A100):**

- Up to ~38% reduction in solve time compared to the previous loop based
implementation.
- Performance gap with native CUDA closes up to ~95%.

Extend velocity calculations to domain boundary faces (#375)

This PR extends the calculation of velocity (Darcy flux) values to the exterior boundary faces of the domain. Here are the highlights:

    Values are calculated for simulations using solver_impes (DirichletBC or FluxBC) or
    solver_richards (all BCs).

    Velocities work with TFG and variable dz options.

    The saturated velocity flux calculation (phase_velocity_face.c) has been added to the
    accelerated library.

    The description of Solver.PrintVelocities in pf-keys/definitions and the manual has been
    augmented with more information.

    Velocity has been added as a test criteria to the following tests from parflow/test/tcl :
    default_single.tcl, default_richards.tcl, default_overland.tcl, and LW_var_dz.tcl

    Also fixes incorrect application of FluxBC in saturated pressure discretization. Previously,
    positive fluxes assigned on a boundary flowed into the domain, and negative fluxes flowed
    out of the domain, regardless of alignment within the coordinate system. The new method
    allows more intuitive flux assignment where positive fluxes move up a coordinate axis and
    negative fluxes move down a coordinate axis.

The tests based on default_richards.tcl have incorrect dimensions/discretization that place some of the boundaries outside the computational domain (default_single.tcl uses the same domain correctly). This prevents any boundary conditions placed on those boundaries from getting invoked. I corrected the discretization and uploaded new PFB files into test/correct_output for the following tests:

- test/tcl/default_overland.tcl
- test/tcl/default_richards.tcl
- test/tcl/default_richards_nocluster.tcl
- test/tcl/default_richards_with_silo.tcl
- test/tcl/van-genuchten-file.tcl

Let me know if changing the tests and regression files is a problem and I'll figure out something else.

Fix OverlandDiffusive BC by restoring temporary vectors for scratch calculations

The OverlandFlowEvalDiff module requires separate temporary vectors (qx, qy)
for its internal calculations. Previous changes removed these local vectors
and passed the State output vectors (q_overlnd_x, q_overlnd_y) directly,
which caused memory corruption issues that manifested as solver failures
with negative slopes in overland_slopingslab_DWE.tcl test.

Solution:
- Restored local temporary vectors qx and qy for OverlandFlowEvalDiff module
- Created new variables q_overlnd_x_ and q_overlnd_y_ pointing to State vectors
- Assign surface fluxes: q_overlnd_x_[io] = ke_[io], q_overlnd_y_[io] = kn_[io]
- This preserves both the module's scratch space needs and our goal of making
  surface flows available to solver_richards.c

########################
## Vegetation forcing ##
########################

Added the option to force the vegetation in CLM (lai, sai, z0m, displa).

A new key is available in the tcl script: ForceVegetation. Default is False. If True, different input files are required depending on whether the meteorological CLM forcing is 1D or 3D:

- 1D forcing case: the user must provide 4 ascii text files (lai.dat, sai.dat, z0m.dat, displa.dat) which contain as many columns (time series) as IGBP vegetation classes (usually 18). The user also provides a vegetation map as a properly distributed pfb file (veg_map.pfb). Values are IGBP vegetation classes that are used to pass 2D maps of lai, sai, displa and z0m from ParFlow to CLM at each timestep.
The vegetation map could be later passed to CLM to remove the dependency on driver files.

- 3D forcing case: the user provides 4 properly distributed 3D (2D + time) files (LAI.pfb, SAI.pfb, Z0M.pfb and DISPLA.pfb) following the same rules as 3D meteorological forcing.

Added test case in the test/clm/ directory: clm_forc_veg.tcl
Added manual entries for this option.

Modified files:
- CLM.F90
- drv_getforce.F90
- solver_richards.c
- parflow_proto_f.h

Changes can be tracked by searching for "BH" flags

########################
## Variable DZ in CLM ##
########################
It has been observed that root fraction distribution in CLM was based on constant DZ, regardless of whether variable DZ was selected in ParFlow. Namely, the call to drv_clmini.F90 occurred before the variable DZ was defined in CLM. This is fixed in this version. The lines defining the root fraction have been copied in CLM.F90 after the variable DZ definition.

However the layer thicknesses and layer interfaces do not match between CLM and ParFlow, only center of cells location match. As a consequence, the volume of the column is not preserved. This has been corrected in this version, and the root fraction distribution is calculated based on layer interfaces which match ParFlow layer interfaces.

Added keys to read DZ multiplier from PFB file for variable DZ runs. Keys are similar to pressure IC:

pfset dzScale.Type                                    PFBFile
pfset dzScale.GeomNames                               <domain>
pfset Geom.domain.dzScale.FileName                    <dzfile>

Added DZ multiplier to CLM call so CLM uses correct DZ values. Note that the DZ variable in CLM 
(clm%dz(k)) is computed between cell centers, whereas ParFlow DZ is between cell interfaces. Anyone
digging deep enough will see that clm%dz(k) in CLM is not equal to dz*dz_mult(k) in ParFlow; however
the values in CLM are consistent with the CLM discretization. 

Also added keys to write CLM variables, EvapTrans, EvapTransSum, OverlandSum, Slopes, and Mannings
as PFB files in addition to Silo. Added key for printing Mask as PFB -- this was set to print based
on PrintSaturation, now it has it's own key. This allows full output without Silo, and lets us undistribute 
output to reduce file count on systems where large numbers of files cause problems. New PFB keys
default to False (except PrintMask, which defaults to True). 

pfset Solver.PrintCLM             False
pfset Solver.PrintSlopes          False
pfset Solver.PrintMannings        False
pfset Sovler.PrintSpecificStorage False
pfset Solver.PrintEvapTrans       False
pfset Solver.PrintEvapTransSum    False
pfset Solver.PrintOverlandSum     False
pfset Solver.PrintOverlandBCFlux  False
pfset Solver.PrintMask            True

Last but not least, created keys to print DZ multiplier (Silo and PFB). 
Defaults are False.

pfset Solver.WriteSiloDZMultiplier False
pfset Solver.PrintDZMultiplier     False

Implemented three irrigation schemes through CLM:

(0) none -- (default)
(1) Spray irrigation -- added to rain rate above veg canopy
(2) Drip irrigation -- added directly to throughfall below canopy
(3) "Instant" irrigation -- artificially sets soil moisture to min(clm%watopt(i),clm%eff_porosity(i))
    (This is the original irrigation scheme from clm_hydro_irrig.F90 and GCM and RCM studies of irrigation's impact on climate)


Irrigation keys are read by solver_richards.c and passed to CLM. 

Solver.CLM.IrrigationType      
 (values: none,Spray,Drip,Instant -- defaults to none)

Solver.CLM.IrrigationCycle     
 (values: Constant, Deficit -- defaults to Constant)
 (Constant cycle applies irrigation each day for IrrigationStartTime <= gmt <= IrrigationStopTime)
 (Deficit cycle applied irrigation based on a soil moisture criteria -- NOT YET IMPLEMENTED)

Solver.CLM.IrrigationRate      
 (rate of irrigation applied at each irrigated timestep, same units as precip (mm/s))

Solver.CLM.IrrigationStartTime 
 (time that irrigation begins each day -- in GMT)

Solver.CLM.IrrigationStopTime
 (time that irrigation is stopped each day -- in GMT)

IrrigationThreshold
 (soil moisture threshold for deficit-based irrigation scheme -- defaults to 0.5)
 (because deficit-based irrigation cycle not yet implemented, this key is not currently used)

Feature: Add IndicatorField netcdf file reading (#710)

## Summary of the PR

This PR was developed to enable the initialization of an IndicatorField
vie a netcdf file, as requested in Issue #651.
This PR includes:
- Code development;
- Documentation on the new key value;
- An example python script as an automated CI test.

---

## On the ParFlow Input Key Convention

The convention for initializing a variable in ParFlow in the input
script is to first set its type using `pfset <Name>.Type` to *Constant*,
*PFBFile* and *NCFile*, after which another key with the expected
`Value` or `FileName`. This convention is followed by boundary condition
keys, `Mannings`, `TopoSlopeX`, `TopoSlopeY`, etc.

As it stands, the initialization of the geometry (including but not
limited to through Indicator Field) does not follow this convention.
Making the proper amendments to the input keys will break every TCL
script to date, and force the users to update them.

With this in mind, this PR proposes another way to allow netcdf files as
input to IndicatorField, via the key `IndicatorFieldNC`. This solution
avoids users having to update their scripts, at the expense that this
key is still not following the same convention as other keys.

---

## Example usage:

In the place of the `IndicatorField` value, the user can opt to write
`IndicatorFieldNC`, after which the code is expecting a key with the
`FileName` for a netcdf file that includes the data for a 3D variable
called "indicator".

```
ifield.GeomInput.indicator_input.InputType = "IndicatorFieldNC"
ifield.GeomInput.indicator_input.GeomNames = "indicator"
ifield.Geom.indicator_input.FileName = "small_domain_indicator_field.nc"
```

The maximum input database value length was increased from 4097 to 65536. A bounds check is performed that emits a helpful error message when a database value is too big.

4097 to 65536 seems like a big increase, but IDB_MAX_VALUE_LEN is only used once as a buffer size to read database entries. The char pointers are then null-terminated and passed to IDB_NewEntry, where strdup mallocs an appropriate string size. The strings are still freed in the same place.

Add SZA-modulated fractional snow cover (FracSnoScheme=SZA) (#709)

## Summary
- Adds a solar zenith angle (SZA) modulated fractional snow cover scheme
as a new option (`FracSnoScheme = "SZA"`) for CLM
- Uses an exponentially-smoothed cosine(SZA) to interpolate effective
roughness between low-sun (near-full cover) and high-sun
(reduced cover) regimes, creating a continuous energy-driven
accumulation/melt asymmetry in fractional snow-covered area (fSCA)
- Fixes a bit-for-bit reproducibility issue in the #701 VIS/NIR snow age
code: at default parameters, the original BATS formula with
hardcoded single-precision literals is now used exactly, avoiding subtle
floating-point differences from the configurable code path

  ## New Keys (5)

  | Key | Default | Description |
  |-----|---------|-------------|
  | `Solver.CLM.FracSnoScheme` | CLM | Extended with `SZA` option |
| `Solver.CLM.FracSnoRoughnessMin` | 1e-8 | Min roughness at low sun [m]
|
| `Solver.CLM.FracSnoRoughnessMax` | 0.2 | Max roughness at high sun [m]
|
  | `Solver.CLM.FracSnoGammaSZA` | 4.0 | Power-law exponent |
| `Solver.CLM.FracSnoAvgWindow` | 72.0 | EMA smoothing window [hours] |

  ## Physics

  coszen_avg ← EMA of max(0, coszen), window = FracSnoAvgWindow hours
  w          = coszen_avg ^ GammaSZA
  z0_eff     = RoughnessMin * (1 - w) + RoughnessMax * w
  frac_sno   = snowdp / (10 * z0_eff + snowdp)

Naturally latitude-aware; no binary mode switches. Default CLM behavior
is completely unchanged.

  ## Files Changed (12 source files)

Add CLM ET formulation improvements: PFT photosynthesis, canopy interception, Medlyn stomata (#712)

## Summary

Fixes CLM3-era ET suppression by addressing four high-priority gaps
identified in the gap analysis (Jefferson et al. 2017, Lawrence et al.
2019):
- **PFT-dependent photosynthesis:** Vcmax 39–62 for forests (vs
hardcoded 33), C4 pathway for grasses/crops, with improved stomata (dark
respiration, smooth colimitation, niter=5). Activated automatically when
`vcmx25` is present in `drv_vegp.dat`.
- **Configurable canopy interception:** `InterceptionFpiMax` (default
0.25) and `FwetExponent` (default 0.6667) keys for CLM3 scheme tuning.
- **CLM5 tanh canopy interception:** `InterceptionScheme=CLM5Tanh` with
`InterceptionTanhAlpha` replaces CLM3's 0.25 ceiling with `fpi = alpha *
tanh(LAI+SAI)`, approaching 1.0 for LAI>2.
- **Medlyn stomatal conductance:** `StomataScheme=Medlyn` uses VPD-based
conductance (Medlyn et al. 2011) with PFT-dependent `g1_medlyn` values
in `drv_vegp.dat`.

All changes are backward-compatible: default key values and existing
`drv_vegp.dat` files reproduce original CLM3 behavior bit-for-bit.

  ## New PF Keys (5)
  | Key | Default | Description |
  |-----|---------|-------------|
| `Solver.CLM.InterceptionFpiMax` | 0.25 | Max interception fraction
(CLM3 scheme) |
  | `Solver.CLM.FwetExponent` | 0.6667 | Wet canopy fraction exponent |
  | `Solver.CLM.StomataScheme` | BallBerry | `BallBerry` or `Medlyn` |
  | `Solver.CLM.InterceptionScheme` | CLM3 | `CLM3` or `CLM5Tanh` |
| `Solver.CLM.InterceptionTanhAlpha` | 1.0 | CLM5 tanh scaling
coefficient |

  ## New drv_vegp.dat parameters (7)

`vcmx25`, `c3psn`, `mp`, `bp`, `qe25`, `folnmx`, `g1_medlyn` — provided
via `drv_vegp_pft.dat`

Presence of `vcmx25` in vegp auto-sets `photosyn_custom=.true.` →
activates improved stomata physics (Rd, smooth colimitation, niter=5).
Old vegp files without these params → original CLM3 defaults →
bit-for-bit.

## Backward compatibility
- `photosyn_custom` boolean flag in `drv_readvegpf.F90` gates improved
stomata (not `isnan()`)
- Guarded fpi/fwet expressions use original Fortran literals at default
key values
  - Original CLM3 stomata loop preserved verbatim in separate code path
- `InterceptionScheme` defaults to `CLM3` → existing fpi code path
unchanged
- New struct fields at END of `clm1d` to preserve existing field offsets

[Enhancement] Improve Umpire Allocator Selection (#669)

**Background**

Previously, ParFlow configured Umpire to always use the `UM_pool
`(Unified Memory) allocator.
While this performs well on NVIDIA GPUs, where Unified Memory provides
efficient page migration and mature driver support, it performs poorly
on AMD MI250X (ROCm) systems.

ROCm’s managed memory (`hipMallocManaged`) still incurs higher paging
and migration overheads, particularly when Heterogeneous Memory
Management (HMM) or XNACK is disabled. In these configurations, managed
allocations fall back to pinned host memory, resulting in slow device
access and degraded solver performance.

**Observations**: When running ParFlow with Kokkos + HIP + Umpire
(`UM_pool`) on AMD MI250X GPUs, initialization completes quickly, but
the KINSOL solver progresses significantly more slowly, leading to
substantial runtime degradation. **NOTE**: This behavior is related to
performance, not numerical convergence or solver correctness.

**Summary of Changes**

This PR refactors Umpire initialization in ParFlow to dynamically select
the most appropriate allocator based on the active Kokkos backend,
improving both performance and portability across GPU architectures.

**Key Updates**

- Allocator Selection Logic
- `UM_pool` used for CUDA (native or Kokkos), SYCL, and OpenMP (Kokkos)
backends
  - `DEVICE_pool` used for HIP (Kokkos) backends
  - `HOST_pool` used as a CPU fallback
- Backend Detection
  - Updated CMake configuration to propagate backend macros:
    - KOKKOS_ENABLE_CUDA
    - KOKKOS_ENABLE_HIP
    - KOKKOS_ENABLE_SYCL
    - KOKKOS_ENABLE_OPENMP_TARGET
- CMake and Logging Cleanup
- Simplified Umpire/RMM messaging now emits a single status line showing
the selected backend and memory manager.
- Log files now report the accelerator backend and the selected memory
pool allocator.
- Expanded Backend Coverage
- Unified logic for native CUDA, Kokkos-enabled CUDA, HIP, SYCL, and
OpenMP Target backends.
  
**Performance Impact**
This update significantly improves GPU performance and portability:

- **AMD MI250X (Kokkos (HIP) )**
Switching from `UM_pool` to `DEVICE_pool` restores expected solver
performance, reducing solvetime to ~25% and total runtime by ~50%
compared to runs without Umpire (i.e., Kokkos(HIP) only).
- **NVIDIA A100 (CUDA / Kokkos (CUDA) )** 
No regressions observed and performance remains consistent with the
previous benchmarks.

**Testing & Verification**

Validated configurations:

- Native CUDA (A100)
- Kokkos-enabled CUDA (A100)
- Kokkos-enabled HIP (MI250X)

Runtime validation confirms:

- Correct allocator selection for each backend
- Stable solver convergence across all configurations
- Expected runtime improvements on AMD GPUs without performance loss on
NVIDIA

This creates a flow barrier capability equivalent to the hydraulic flow barrier (HFB) or flow and transport parameters at interfaces. The flow barriers are placed at the fluxes as scalar multipliers between cells (at cell interfaces). The following things were added to the code:

    three new vectors to store the FB values in X, Y and Z
    problem modules for each vector, (currently the values are only loaded as PFB files but this could be expanded in the future)
    modification to the function evaluation and jacobian for the flow barrier formulation
    two test cases in the test suite
    additions to the manual describing the physics and usage of this feature

The flow barrier boolean default to False, which sets the values to unity, thus providing backward compatibility.

Fix build with CUDA 13 and latest toolchains (#705)

## Overview

This PR restores ParFlow build compatibility with recent versions of its
optional backends and dependencies:

- CUDA 13  
- RMM ≥ 25.06  
- Umpire ≥ 2025.09  
- Tcl 9*

These versions introduce API and toolchain requirements (notably C++17)
that prevent successful compilation with the current build
configuration.

*Minimal changes applied to restore compilation.

**NOTE**

- The changes are limited to compatibility adjustments.  
- No algorithmic or performance changes are introduced.
---

## Changes

### 1. C++17 enablement

Enable C++17 when required by:

- CUDA 13 / libcu++
- RMM ≥ 25.06
- Umpire ≥ 2025.09

Compatibility with older toolchains and dependency versions is
preserved.

---

### 2. CUDA 13 compatibility

- Update `cudaMemPrefetchAsync` calls to use `cudaMemLocation` as
required by CUDA 13.
- Adapt to the CUB `BlockReduce` template signature change (explicit
architecture template parameter removed in CUDA 13).

These updates resolve compilation errors under CUDA 13.  
No functional changes are introduced.

---

### 3. RMM header layout

Update include paths to reflect the current RMM header structure
(`rmm/mr/`). Compatibility with older versions is preserved.

---

### 4. Tcl 9 compatibility

Replace `int` size parameters with `Tcl_Size` where required by Tcl 9.

**Note**: While ParFlow compiles with Tcl 9, `pftools` require
additional updates due to broader Tcl 9 scripting changes. Further
details are provided in migration guide:
https://core.tcl-lang.org/tcl/wiki?name=Migrating+scripts+to+Tcl+9.

_This may be a suitable point to discuss full transition to Python (see
issue #641)._

---

## Tested Configurations

### Modern stack

- CUDA 13.0.48  
- GCC 14.3.0  
- Tcl 9.0.1  
- Umpire 2025.09.0  
- RMM 25.12.00  

### Backward-compatible stack

- CUDA 12.6.20  
- GCC 13.3.0  
- Tcl 8.6.14  
- Umpire 2024.07.0  
- RMM 24.12.01  

Build and runtime validated on both configurations.

---

## Scope

- Minimal API and build-system adjustments  
- No changes to numerical methods or runtime behavior  
- Restores compatibility with current CUDA/C++17-based HPC environments

Sign convention for top flux boundary conditions and EvapTrans files

Top flux boundary conditions (e.g., OverlandFlow, SeepageFace) and EvapTrans files do not follow the same sign convention:

- Top flux boundary conditions require a sign flip (i.e., outgoing fluxes are positive): [Evidence: default_overland.tcl](https://github.com/parflow/parflow/blob/master/test/tcl/default_overland.tclL308))
- EvapTrans files do not require a sign flip (i.e., outgoing fluxes are negative): [Evidence: overland_flux.tcl](https://github.com/parflow/parflow/blob/master/test/tcl/overland_flux.tcl#L322)

I specified this information in the respective keys. I also specified that EvapTrans files are expected to be ParFlow 3D binary files.

Refactor allocation of Overland variables (#619)

This PR addresses an issue brought up during the core ParFlow developer
meeting of June 9th, 2025.

In summary, there were identified a combined total of 16 variables in
the main `NlFunctionEval()` and `RichardsJacobianEval()` modules that
were allocated and deallocated at every invoke call of the modules,
which can happen multiple times in each nonlinear iteration.
Additionally, most of these variables are only used when a boundary
condition (BC) of the type OverlandFlow is active.

Therefore, this PR introduces a few updates:
1. Moves variable allocation outside of the iteration loop;
2. Only allocates variables when OverlandFlow-type BCs are active;
3. Achieves performance gains in solver time around 12% for problems
without OverlandFlow;
4. Achieves performance gains in solver time around 8% for problems with
OverlandFlow;
5. Achieves small memory savings for problems without OverlandFlow.

Update overlandflow_eval_Kin.c (#603)

Fix to overlandflow_eval_Kin to correct issue with overland surface boundary and Dirichlet side boundary.

The issue is with the “top” pressure value. The top function is used here
[k1y = pfmax((int)top_dat[itop + sy_v],0);](https://github.com/parflow/parflow/blob/483aac5603f6ad69f04e1a12faf5f84859ff5ea6/pfsimulator/parflow_lib/overlandflow_eval_Kin.c#L139)
[to get the upwinded pressure](https://github.com/parflow/parflow/blob/483aac5603f6ad69f04e1a12faf5f84859ff5ea6/pfsimulator/parflow_lib/overlandflow_eval_Kin.c#L156).

The top value is zero and we are counting on the pressures outside the active domain being zero. I actually don’t think they always are, I think the BC information gets inserted into the inactive cells adjacent to the boundary and this value at k=0 is what’s being used any time the slopes point into the domain. This fix checks for the upper right and
upper upper top values, if they are <0 (meaning outside the active domain) it assigns an upper pressure of zero, otherwise it assigns the pressure from the upper or right cells (north and east cells) as normal.

Feature/Integrate PDI Interface enhancements (#590)

**Overview**

This pull request integrates PDI interface enhancements, originally
developed in `parflow-pdi` (a GitLab fork of Parflow), into the latest
Parflow codebase. The implementation follows
[PDI](https://pdi.dev/main/index.html) guidelines and introduces new
functionality to support in-situ data processing and analysis.

**What is PDI?**

For more details, please refer to the [PDI GitHub
repository](https://github.com/pdidev/pdi/tree/main?tab=readme-ov-file#the-pdi-distribution),
where it is described as:

> "PDI is a library that aims to decouple high-performance simulation
codes from input/output concerns. It offers a declarative API that
enables codes to expose the buffers in which they store data and to
notify PDI of significant simulation steps. Additionally, it supports a
plugin system to make existing libraries such as HDF5, NetCDF, or Python
available to codes—potentially mixing several in a single execution."

**Implemented Features**

Current iteration implemented the following PDI features:

- Per-Process Data Collection: Each process collects simulation data
independently.
- HDF5 File Output: Data is saved to HDF5 files with filenames that
include the corresponding process rank.

**Future Enhancements**

- In-Transit Data Processing: Future iterations will focus on in-transit
data processing and analysis, reducing the need for disk I/O operations.

**What This PR Does**

This PR lays the foundation for integrating PDI into Parflow, and aims
to initiate discussions around the current implementation and future
development of in-situ data processing capabilities.

- Upstream Sync: Merges the latest changes from `parflow-pdi`, ensuring
compatibility with current upstream developments.
- PDI Interface Integration: Adds new components and modifications
necessary for PDI support.
- Conflict Resolution & Refactoring: Updates existing modules to address
conflicts and align with upstream code changes.
- Temporary Directory Structure: Configuration file for PDI
specification tree (defining data types and plugin lists) and output
testing files are currently located in a dedicated `pdi/` directory.

* CMake vars uppercase, restore RMM_ROOT, update GPU docs (#694)

### Summary

This PR standardizes CMake variable naming and updates GPU
documentation. It addresses a breaking configuration change where
`RMM_ROOT`, originally defined in uppercase, was later changed to
mixed-case (`rmm_ROOT`), which silently broke existing user build
scripts when upgrading ParFlow. This PR restores the original uppercase
convention and enforces consistent naming across all third-party
dependencies to prevent similar regressions.

### Changes

- **CMake variable consistency:**
  - All third-party CMake variables are now uppercase, including:
    - `RMM_ROOT` (restored from mixed-case `rmm_ROOT`)
    - `UMPIRE_ROOT` (updated from `umpire_ROOT`)
- This aligns with existing variables such as `KOKKOS_ROOT`,
`SILO_ROOT`, `HYPER_ROOT`, and `SUNDIALS_ROOT`.
- **Workflow files** updated to reflect the uppercase RMM_ROOT and
UMPIRE_ROOT variables.
- **Backward compatibility fix:**
- `RMM_ROOT` was originally uppercase; changing it to lowercase silently
broke existing user scripts when upgrading to newer ParFlow versions.
This PR restores the original convention to avoid unexpected build
failures.
- **Documentation updates (README-GPU.md):**
- Removed obsolete references to RMM v0.10 and the previous upgrade
work-in-progress note
  - Ensured consistent use of `RMM_ROOT`
  - Updated the RMM link to the official repository

Extends CLM snow parameterizations with new rain-snow partitioning
methods, SZA-based melt damping, and configurable fractional snow cover.

- **Dai (2008) rain-snow partitioning**: Hyperbolic tangent function
fitted to 30 years of global observations
- **Jennings (2018) rain-snow partitioning**: Bivariate logistic
regression using temperature and relative humidity

Added DEM processing routines to pftools

 pfslopex dem
 Calculates slopes in x-direction using 1st order upwind finite differences
 For local maxima, slope is maximum downward gradient (towards lowest neighbor in x-direction)
 For local minima, slope is set to zero (no drainage in x-direction)
 NOTE: function uses dx value from dem data structure -- must be set correctly!

 pfslopey dem
 Calculates slopes in y-direction using 1st order upwind finite differences
 For local maxima, slope is maximum downward gradient (towards lowest neighbor in y-direction)
 For local minima, slope is set to zero (no drainage in y-direction)
 NOTE: function uses dy value from dem data structure -- must be set correctly!

 pfupstreamarea sx sy
 Calculates upstream contributing area at all cells. 
 Area is returned as NUMBER OF CELLS, not as an actual area.

 pfpitfilldem dem dpit maxiter
 Iterates over DEM to fill sinks using simple pit-fill.
 At each iteration, locates sinks cells with sx==sy==0.0 *or* elevation less than all neighboring cells.
 Adds dpit to elevation at sink. Iterates until all sinks are full or maxiter is reached. 

 pfsetgrid {nx ny nz} {x0 y0 z0} {dx dy dz} dataset
 Simple utility function that sets the grid information of dataset to the values provided.

Fix missing Ippisch modification in interior cell Kr evaluation

The interior cell loop (GrGeomInLoop for "Compute rel. perms. on
interior") was not modified with the Ippisch air-entry check and
scaling. This caused the direct-eval path to compute standard VG Kr
for interior cells while the table path correctly computed Ippisch Kr,
leading to divergent solver behavior (different Newton iterations and
pressure fields of ~130 difference).

Fix applies the same Ippisch modification (h_s air-entry check,
ippisch_fac scaling, adjusted table index for linear interpolation)
to all four interior loop paths: CALCFCN direct, CALCFCN linear,
CALCDER direct, CALCDER linear.

Verified: table vs direct now gives identical iterations and field
differences < 1e-9 for both n=1.5 and n=2.0 Ippisch cases.

  domain starts at h_s instead of 0

Compiling parflow with the Intel-OneAPI compiler throws the following
warning:

pfmask-to-pfsol.cpp:444:6: warning: comparison with NaN always evaluates
to false in fast floating point modes [-Wtautological-constant-compare]
  if(isnan(dx))

early warn TCL support deprecate and Tcl 9.x warning (#716)

## Summary

Marks TCL support as deprecated and adds early version-gating for the
Tcl 9.x incompatibility for generating PFIDB, replacing silent runtime
failures with configure-time warnings.

## Changes

- Issue a deprecation `WARNING` when TCL is found, directing users to
Python-based
  pftools and tracking issue #707
- Raise a `WARNING` when Tcl ≥ 9.0 is detected as generating PFIDB is
unsupported on that version

## Motivation

Tcl 9.x silently breaks at runtime and does not generate PFIDB, with no
configure-time indication, leading to hard-to-diagnose failures. This
change surfaces the incompatibility immediately at configure time and
consistently nudges remaining TCL users toward the Python migration path
ahead of eventual removal.

## Testing

- [x] **Configured with Tcl 8.6:** deprecation warning issued, build
proceeds normally
- [x] **Configured with Tcl 9.0:** both warnings issued, build proceeds
with known limitations noted

-  #707

Activate EvapTrans without CLM compilation

- In TSMP we cannot use EvapTrans as ParFlow must be compiled with
  CLM to use this option. However, we need this in TSMP to simulate
  e.g. human water consumption. As EvapTrans works fine even without
  CLM compiled, we can simply move the routine that reads in the
  EvapTrans forcing file outside the `ifdef HAVE_CLM` option.
  To ensure no interference if CLM is compiled, all relevant changes
  are placed in `ifndef HAVE_CLM' compiler flags to be used only if
  CLM is not compiled.
- Change coupling behaviour to not replace `evap_trans` in ParFlow
  with OASIS (=), but to add the fields sent by CLM (+=). This way
  EvapTrans and CLM coupling can be used together and the forcing
  is summed up for ParFlow.
- It is ensured that the above changes do not introduce additional
  mandatory forcing files as `evap_trans` is initialised to 0 and
  reset at the beginning of each time loop.

Replace octree iteration with box iteration. (#148)

The octree loop iteration was replaced with iteration over a simple array of boxes that cover the geometry. For backward compatibility, the new clustering method can be turned off with the UseClustering input key.

The octree loop iteration was not very efficient. For example a flat plane of data (surface) was causing iterations into 1x1x1 leaf nodes in the octree due to power of 2 spatial division that is inherent to a standard octree representation of space. To compute the set of boxes, the Berger-Rigoutsos algorithm is run on a set of tags setup using the octree. This will compute a reasonably efficient set of boxes for iteration. For example, the top surface is now a single box if top is a uniform single geometry. Based on tests run on larger problem this is always more efficient. For very small problems the BR algorithm cost can be larger than loop savings.

This change should also be helpful for the work going with accelerators since the iteration will be over larger sized patches.

Add Kokkos support for accelerators (#327)

This PR adds Kokkos accelerator backend as an alternative to the native ParFlow CUDA backend to support more accelerator devices. The implementation does not rely on any CUDA-specific arguments but still requires Unified Memory support from the accelerator devices. It should be compatible with AMD GPUs when sufficient Unified Memory support is available from this vendor.

The performance of using CUDA through the Kokkos library is slightly worse in comparison to the ParFlow native CUDA implementation. This is because a general Kokkos implementation cannot leverage certain CUDA features such as cudaMemset() for initializations or CUDA pinned host/device memory for MPI buffers. Also, Kokkos determines grid and block sizes for compute kernels differently.

The RMM pool allocator for Unified Memory can be used with Kokkos (when using Kokkos CUDA backend) and improves the performance very significantly. In the future, a Unified Memory pool allocator that supports AMD cards is likely needed to achieve good performance.

User instructions on how to use Kokkos backend can be found from README-GPU.md. Basically, the following must be specified for CMake when compiling ParFlow:

-DPARFLOW_ACCELERATOR_BACKEND=kokkos -DKokkos_ROOT=/path/to/Kokkos

Furthermore, the performance of the simulation initialization phase has been improved significantly when using GPUs (with CUDA and Kokkos).

Update hydrology.py (#429)

Bugfix in Python PFtools  _overland_flow_kinematic method, the formulation in this patch matches the outflow of ParFlow along the edges of irregular domains, which the prior Hydrology Python PFTools did not.

a) the slope in both x and y are corrected (by copying the corresponding value inside the mask) outside the mask edges in lower x and y as they both come into play through "slope".
b) because the correction is now done at lower x and y edges in both slopex and slopey, this could lead to overwriting the slopes outside for grid cells that are both outside x and y lower edges. For this, the calculation in x (q_x, qeast) is done first, after adjusting slopes outside lower x edges and then the calculation in y (q_y, qnorth) is done second, after adjusting slopes outside lower y edges.

Sign convention for top flux boundary conditions and EvapTrans files (#469)

Top flux boundary conditions (e.g., OverlandFlow, SeepageFace) and
EvapTrans files do not follow the same sign convention:

- Top flux boundary conditions require a sign flip (i.e., outgoing
fluxes are positive) ~ Evidence:
[default_overland.tcl](https://github.com/parflow/parflow/blob/master/test/tcl/default_overland.tclL308))
- EvapTrans files do not require a sign flip (i.e., outgoing fluxes are
negative) ~ Evidence:
[overland_flux.tcl](https://github.com/parflow/parflow/blob/master/test/tcl/overland_flux.tcl#L322)

I specified this information in the respective keys. I also specified
that EvapTrans files are expected to be ParFlow 3D binary files.

Add isotropic diffusion correction for OverlandKinematic

Adds an optional diffusion correction to the kinematic wave overland
flow formulation: delta_q = -D * grad(psi), where D = alpha * |psi|^{5/3}
/ (n * |Sf|^{1/2}) and Sf = S0 + grad(psi) (friction slope). The
correction smooths water surfaces on flat terrain, lake edges, and
backwater zones where the kinematic approximation is weakest.

Implementation:
- Single-file C change to overlandflow_eval_Kin.c (CALCFCN + CALCDER)
- Two Jacobian options: Picard (simple, robust) and FullNewton (faster
  convergence, includes dD/dpsi terms)
- Default off: produces bit-identical results when disabled
- Inherits all kinematic boundary handling (patch edges, lower boundaries)

New keys:
- Solver.OverlandKinematic.DiffusionCorrection.Type: None | Isotropic
- Solver.OverlandKinematic.DiffusionCorrection.Alpha: strength (0-1)
- Solver.OverlandKinematic.DiffusionCorrection.Jacobian: Picard | FullNewton

Also includes:
- pftools hydrology module: OverlandKinematicDiffusive flow method
- User manual: equations, key reference, Python API documentation
- Test cases: tilted-V (3 configs) and sloping slab (4 directions)
- Comparison visualization script

maintenance overhead.

references to local version of CUB.

Fix integer overflow in large dataset databox allocation and indexing (#700)

This PR incorporates work originally done by @skollet [Stefan
Kollet](https://github.com/skollet) to fix integer overflow in databox
allocation and pointer arithmetic that could lead to segmentation faults
when handling large PFB files, e.g., when running `pfdist`. The changes
switch indexing and allocation to `size_t`, replace raw `calloc` with
`ctalloc`, and correct offset calculations in I/O paths, ensuring safe
handling of large grids.


**Note**

This PR addresses integer overflow in Databox allocation and selected
indexing paths. However, it is a partial fix. A follow-up issue has been
opened to track full migration of indexing and allocation to `size_t`
across all operations: Issue #703.

Add Denominator and FullNewtonDdx options for diffusion correction

Three denominator choices for D in the diffusion correction:
- BedSlope (default): D uses |S_0|, ATS-style, needs epsilon floor
- FrictionSlope: D uses |S_f| = |S_0 + alpha*grad(psi)|, self-regularizing
- Pythagorean: D uses sqrt(|S_0|^2 + |alpha*grad(psi)|^2), self-regularizing
  with smoother Jacobian (dD/dhx -> 0 on steep terrain)

New Jacobian option FullNewtonDdx (Level 2): adds dD/d(grad_psi) terms
through the face-parallel gradient only, staying 5-point stencil.
Only active for FrictionSlope/Pythagorean denominators.

    potentially reducing the number of solver iterations, particularly the
    function evaluations. Keys are added to the database and RST files,
    feature defaults as false so baseline functionality is unchanged and
    backward compatibility is preserved.

    <runname>.Solver.SurfacePredictor.PrintValues = True [False]
    <runname>.Solver.SurfacePredictor.PressureValue = [0.00001]

    Bugfix in Python PFtools  _overland_flow_kinematic method, the formulation in this patch matches the outflow of ParFlow along the edges of irregular domains, which the prior Hydrology Python PFTools did not.

    a) the slope in both x and y are corrected (by copying the corresponding value inside the mask) outside the mask edges in lower x and y as they both come into play through "slope".
    b) because the correction is now done at lower x and y edges in both slopex and slopey, this could lead to overwriting the slopes outside for grid cells that are both outside x and y lower edges. For this, the calculation in x (q_x, qeast) is done first, after adjusting slopes outside lower x edges and then the calculation in y (q_y, qnorth) is done second, after adjusting slopes outside lower y edges.

Fix bug in run.dist() (#536)

run.dist() does not re-distribute well files that have been already been
distributed in a way that p, q, r do not exactly divide NX, NY, NZ. The
problem lies in trying to "estimate" p, q, r when reading those
distributed files in with the ParflowBinaryReader.

This pull request removes the precomputation option (which cannot work
if we allow distributing grids unevenly), and adds explicit calculation
for p, q, r in the read_subgrid_info. Also, a test for
ParflowBinaryReader is added, which distributes and redistributes a pfb
file. That test fails with the previous implementation.

compressible storage positive (#566)

The subsurface storage computation previously allowed negative storage
values when the pressure head was negative, potentially leading to
physically unrealistic results. This issue occurred in both the Python
and Tcl pftools scripts. To address this, a minimum value of zero has
been imposed for compressible storage in both scripts, ensuring that
negative storage values are avoided. The implementation is backward
compatible and should not affect existing workflows.

GPU integration into amps mpi1 layer (+minor updates) (#280)

This PR integrates GPU capabilities into mpi1 amps layer with a cleaner implementation and better performance and error handling over the earlier amps cuda layer. The GPU packing functions are contained in a separate amps_gpupacking.cu file. By default, GPU packing is used, but CPU pointers are passed to the MPI library such that CUDA-aware MPI library is not required. A runtime environment variable PARFLOW_USE_GPUDIRECT=1 disables host staging and enables GPU pointers to be passed to MPI library improving performance (but requires a CUDA-aware MPI library). Amps cuda layer becomes deprecated and may be removed in the future to reduce code duplication and maintenance burden.
List of changes:

    Integrate GPU capabilities into mpi1 layer
    Fix amps smpi layer compile issues
    Fix amps smpi layer memory leak (persistent MPI_Requests not freed)
    Fix amps cuda layer memory leak (persistent MPI_Requests not freed)
    Disable unified memory use in clustering.c to improve performance
    Add CUDA 11 support

- if using a modifier Key like Shift, Control and ALT you can´t rely on the result of the corresponding event (e.g KeyEvent, MouseEvent), it is always 0

The situation is stranger if more than one modifier is needed. 
QApplication::keyboardModifiers() == Qt::ShiftModifier & QApplication::keyboardModifiers() == Qt::ControlModifier 
will not work.
Instead use Qt::KeyboardModifiers keyMod = Qt::keyboardModifiers()
and then keyMod.testFlag(e.g. Qt::ControlModifier)

Register plugin function

Plugins can register themselves by passing a plugin instance and version to registerPlugin. The purpose of this is to ensure that only the newest ever loaded plugin will be kept.
K saves all successfully registered plugins into pluginDir, holds all registered plugins in registeredPlugins and running registered plugins in runningPlugins.
When loading a plugin with the same name as an already running plugin, a version check is done and the newer one is kept.
If a plugin with the same name is registered but not running, it is run first before running the newly loaded plugin to ensure that the version check will happen.

The signal slot system allows for signals to be connected to slots
with less arguments than the signal provides,
leftover args are discarded.
The new recentering position slot accepts one coordinate argument
whereas the old signals provide 3 components as individual args.

using its first ctor, which equalized all components with the arg.

also, VIEWPORT_UNDEFINED was used to ctor the normal vector for userMove

The ctor was intended to offer all math operations on vectors also
to scalars, a scalar arg could be used to construct a coordinate
which could then be used with vector operations.

The problematic ctor has been removed
and all scalar operations have been implemented seperately.

Register plugin function

Plugins can register themselves by passing a plugin instance and version to registerPlugin. The purpose of this is to ensure that only the newest ever loaded plugin will be kept.
K saves all successfully registered plugins into pluginDir, holds all registered plugins in registeredPlugins and running registered plugins in runningPlugins.
When loading a plugin with the same name as an already running plugin, a version check is done and the newer one is kept.
If a plugin with the same name is registered but not running, it is run first before running the newly loaded plugin to ensure that the version check will happen.
